title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DANA'S GUITAR
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Dana Whitfield, a forty-one-year-old night-shift package sorter in Memphis, Tennessee.
She had never played one note of music. But her dad Earl played guitar on Beale Street for thirty years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PAWN SHOP
segments.quote: The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: Every morning after work, Dana walked past a pawn shop with a red guitar in the window. Sixty dollars.
Every morning she told herself, you're forty-one. Keep walking.
Then she remembered a line from Oscar Wilde, the Irish wit:
The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.
She yielded. The man threw in a tuner, out of pity.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: SORE FINGERS
segments.quote: Practice means to perform over and over again, in the face of all obstacles, some act of vision, of faith, of desire.
segments.author: Martha Graham
lines: Her plan: play Happy Birthday at Earl's seventy-second birthday, three months away.
Her fingertips burned, and every chord sounded like a cat in a screen door.
A lesson video opened with the dancer Martha Graham:
Practice means to perform over and over again, in the face of all obstacles, some act of vision, of faith, of desire.
So she practiced twenty minutes every night. Sore fingers and all.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PROS
segments.quote: Every artist was first an amateur.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: Then she watched a guy online play faster than her sorting belt. Under the bed it went.
Her supervisor Luis taped a note to her scanner, from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Every artist was first an amateur.
That guy started with sore fingers too. The guitar came back out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WRONG NOTE
segments.quote: A man of genius makes no mistakes. His errors are volitional and are the portals of discovery.
segments.author: James Joyce
lines: Two weeks out, she hit the same wrong chord every single time.
Her coworker Pete, who reads very thick books at lunch, quoted James Joyce:
A man of genius makes no mistakes. His errors are volitional and are the portals of discovery.
Volitional means on purpose. So Dana kept it, and called it her Memphis twist.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BACKYARD
segments.quote: A great deal of talent is lost to the world for the want of a little courage.
segments.author: Sydney Smith
lines: On the big night, forty relatives packed Earl's backyard. Dana's hands shook.
She almost said she'd left it in the car.
Then Aunt Bernice whispered a line from Sydney Smith, an English wit:
A great deal of talent is lost to the world for the want of a little courage.
Dana stood up and played. Memphis twist and all.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PORCH
segments.quote: After silence, that which comes nearest to expressing the inexpressible is music.
segments.author: Aldous Huxley
lines: Nobody spoke. Then Earl held out his hands for the guitar.
His fingers were stiff, but he played his old Beale Street blues, and Dana followed.
Her mom, wiping her eyes, quoted the writer Aldous Huxley:
After silence, that which comes nearest to expressing the inexpressible is music.
Now they play every Sunday on his porch. The neighbors bring chairs.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Yield to the good temptation. Practice. Start as an amateur. Keep your twist. Find courage. Let music talk.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Yield to the good temptation. Practice. Start as an amateur. Keep your wrong notes. Find a little courage. Let the music talk.
I tried the trumpet once. My neighbors still thank me for stopping.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
